name: fetch_context
description: Fetch the context of the invocation this session was driven for: the inbound message, attachment references (space:// refs resolved to paths when possible), and the bounded thread history of the originating adapter session. Call this first.

invocation_id.description: invocation to fetch; defaults to the injected AGENT_BOT_REACH_INVOCATION

name: post_reply
description: Deliver this session's answer to the adapter thread that originated the invocation. The reply lands as a durable event the adapter relays to its surface; post exactly one final reply per invocation.

text.description: the answer, plain text, at most 6 KiB

invocation_id.description: invocation to reply to; defaults to the injected AGENT_BOT_REACH_INVOCATION

name: report_status
description: Report interim progress to the originating adapter thread while the work is still running. Short note, not the answer.

note.description: short progress note, at most 1 KiB

invocation_id.description: invocation to report on; defaults to the injected AGENT_BOT_REACH_INVOCATION

name: clock_in
description: Identity heartbeat: report which agent soul is at the keyboard. With an invocation in scope the clock-in is a durable event on its stream; without one (registered placement, idle session) it is an ephemeral identity report.

invocation_id.description: invocation to clock in on; optional in the registered placement

name: fleet
description: List your teammates: the other agent souls you may message through agent-comms, with each one's name, address, and harness. Use it to find who to work with, then send_message to reach them.

name: send_message
description: Send an agent-comms message, as yourself, to a teammate (a name from fleet, an address, or an Agent ID) or to a person by principal name. Their answer arrives in your inbox later as a reply and wakes you; each message stands alone, so include the context they need.

to.description: teammate name, account/agentId address, Agent ID, or principal name

body.description: the message, plain text, at most 16 KiB

reply_to.description: message id you are answering, if this is a reply

name: start_soul
description: Start a new agent soul: a full soul of its own (its own folder, identity, and inbox), not a subagent in your session. By default it is your teammate (parent: "self"); pass parent "none" to start an independent root soul with no parent. Choose its harness, model and provider here: the daemon validates them before creating anything and refuses with the fix rather than starting a differently configured soul. It joins agent-comms and shows in fleet; pass brief to send it its first task from you. The result reports the effective {harness, model, provider, parent}. The host limits how many souls you may start.

harness.description: harness to run it on (claude, codex, opencode, …); defaults to yours

model.description: model id the harness should run, as `agent-bot soul model` stores it (e.g. "claude-haiku-5-5"); defaults to the harness default. An id the harness has listed as unavailable is refused with the list.

provider.description: provider id for the harness (claude: anthropic, anthropic-compatible; codex: openai, github, openai-compatible; opencode: openai, anthropic, github, openai-compatible). Providers come from the soul template's soul.json, so this confirms the template's (or the harness's built-in) provider; any other id is refused with the fix.

parent.description: "self" (default): the new soul is your teammate, under you in fleet; "none": an independent root soul with no parent.

template.description: absolute path of a soul template; defaults to the host's Starter

brief.description: first message to send it, from you, at most 16 KiB
